body: This feels more like a feature rhan a strict bugfix, so not sure it's appropriate for a new contributor, see [our policy](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#no-features-from-new-contributors)
Oh not disputing it is a fix, but rather the scope and scale of it for a new contributor

> Oh not disputing it is a fix, but rather the scope and scale of it for a new contributor

New contributors to Godot do not necessarily lack programming experience or experience in submitting pull requests. Honestly, I find it quite strange that submitting a functional PR requires a certain level of seniority. Now, even fixing PRs requires completing some kind of KPI before they can be submitted?

> so not sure it's appropriate for a new contributor

In that case, some recently merged PRs should be reverted and then re-merged once the authors have sufficient seniority, such as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115426

I didn't close this PR nor did I say it should be closed, I simply informed about this policy so the author is aware in case the relevant teams consider that it violates this policy

PRs made before the new policy are excempt in some cases

As we discussed in the issue thread, this is the way to go. But we can actually avoid changing the signatures from the C# side.

Take the following method as an example:

```cs
public static partial godot_string godotsharp_variant_as_string(scoped in godot_variant p_self);
```

This method is not actually a P/Invoke method, but a wrapper to a generated method that invokes the actual native one. This is needed because by-ref parameters (`in`, `ref`, and `out`) cannot be used in native calls, so [our internal source generator converts them to pointers](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34d06658a85845111a50db9e485ec4a0701d4298/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/Godot.SourceGenerators.Internal/UnmanagedCallbacksGenerator.cs#L339-L344).
The same thing could be done with return types. If the return type is not one of a select few list of approved ones, then it gets converted into a pointer parameter appended at the end.
This way we wouldn't need to change anything from the C# side and we won't need to break expressions into multiple statements.

I'm also really interested in this.

For easier work with the style checks you can install `prek` locally https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/introduction.html#setting-up-a-dev-environment, with this it's easier to pass the CI.

Edit: After compiling to WASM in a proof-of-concept PR with LibGodot `godotsharp_variant_as_string`, `godotsharp_variant_as_string_name`, `godotsharp_variant_as_node_path`, and `godotsharp_variant_as_rid` caused `RuntimeError: function signature mismatch` when they were called which I think is caused by the same issue.

Just a heads up, I was messing around this PR and there seems to be some inconsistencies in referencing the array_new_mem_copy functions in memnew_placement.

And others like this:
https://github.com/Raphtaliyah/godot/blob/c109a46f6dff6fd96afb84e8448692ce9ab1f6c5/modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp#L416

It caused a couple of compiler warnings on my end, but at this moment my build is really messy and I can't tell if the root cause are those inconsistencies.

Hi there!
Sorry for the absence, hopefully the extra things I did make up for it! :)

I did "read" the guidelines and skipped right past the "No features from new contributors" section, since I wasn't adding a new feature. Maybe changing the title to include "... or significant re-factoring ..." or moving it to its own section would be better! Maybe I could contribute that to increase my merged PRs! :)
In all honesty: that policy seems a bit weird. As others have said it (thanks @scgm0), new contributor doesn't mean new to programming and I have experience in these things.

Small things that changed:
* I rebased the PR onto the latest commit, it should merge cleanly.
* Fixed small merge conflicts (like `LipO::create_file` going `static`).
* Updated the new things that touched what my PR also touches. For example, in the `gd_mono_cache.h`: a `class_name` got introduced in the "old" format, so that got updated as well (and in the managed side in `ScriptManagerBridge.cs` as well).
* Fixed the formatting issues in my original code (and hopefully didn't cause more, I added `prek` so it should be fine going forward).
* @Hex27 was right! There was indeed a mistake in my code, I left two address-of operators! That's now cleaned up.

The big ones: Source generator!

The source generator used ids like `GODOT-INTERNAL-G000x`, which aren't valid. They have to be valid C# identifiers, and they only fail once actually encountered. This likely means no one encountered a `GODOT-INTERNAL-G0001` or a `GODOT-INTERNAL-G0002` before!
The public diagnostics use `GDxxxx` style ids, so I changed them to `GDI` (as in "Godot Internal"). I needed to add a new diagnostic, so I had to do something about it, normally I would have made this its own PR. If these are documented anywhere, and this ends up becoming their actual name, they should be updated.

I took @neikeq's advice and moved this into the source generator! `UnmanagedCallbacksGenerator` now generates the return pointer conversion instead of having to deal with it manually. This also means I reverted a lot of the original C# code as it became unnecessary, and has the upside of the API staying the same (not really, more on that later, I found more things!).

The source generator now unconditionally uses the `<type> ret = _unmanagedCallbacks.<func>(...);` and `return ret;` pattern for anything not `void` returning. This has no functional or performance change, the JIT should generate the exact same code, but if anyone relied on diffs, this could be noticed (and that's probably the highest consequence I can think of: being "noticed"). This allowed me to simplify the code generation before complicating it.
There is now a helper `ShouldPassReturnThrough(ITypeSymbol type)` which decides if a return type can be used for interop without anything else or needs special care. (The `IsIllegalReturnType(ITypeSymbol type)` can be ignored for now, that's, confusingly, for the diagnostic.)

If there is no special care needed, the resulting code is very similar. The pointer is `delegate* unmanaged<{PARAMETERS}, {RETURN TYPE}> ...` and the code is (assuming no code between call and return, that part always existed but now works implicitly):
```
{RETURN TYPE} ret = _unmanagedCallbacks.{FUNCTION}({PARAMETERS});
return ret;
```

If special care is needed, the pointer becomes `delegate* unmanaged<{PARAMETERS}, {RETURN TYPE}*, void> ...` and the code becomes:
```
{RETURN TYPE} ret = default;
_unmanagedCallbacks.{FUNCTION}({PARAMETERS}, &ret);
return ret;
```

It also handles functions having no parameters (so `&ret` instead of `, &ret`) and the like. I think I managed to keep generated code formatting consistent as well.

While doing this I discovered more issues in the interop layer: `bool` was being passed through (in GodotTools this time). `bool` and `char` looks like they should be regular unmanaged blittable types you can pass through, but no: they require marshalling (and Godot doesn't have runtime marshalling disabled). Neither should be used as a parameter or return type (and can't be used as a return type anymore).
To fix this, the source generator gained a new diagnostic `GDI0003`! (In `Common.cs`.) This is an error raised when the return type of an interop method is `bool`, `char` or a managed type. The first two can't be reliably passed through in a platform agnostic way, and the third can't have its address taken (and if it had, that would crash under GC). This is checked by the helper `IsIllegalReturnType`, and if it returns `true` this error is raised on the offending function.

So then, why does `ShouldPassReturnThrough` allow these types? You can't "abort" source generation cleanly, doing so would leave unimplemented partial methods, which would raise their own errors and spam the output. To avoid this, the code currently emitts "valid" code that would behave incorrectly, which is fine, since the diagnostic is an error so nothing gets compiled, and only `GDI0003` is emitted. I don't like this solution but anything cleaner requires more refactoring, which doesn't belong in this PR, and the source generator uses the older `ISourceGenerator`, so if I would put more work into this, I would rather just migrate the whole generator.

This new diagnostic flagged the offending places (only `bool`s), and I updated them in GodotTools as well. I feel like this still belongs into this PR, since it just continues what I started, but it, admittedly, got pretty fat. This ended up being the only API change in the managed code.

As a note: I didn't want to overdo it, so I only made it catch illegal return types, but these types are illegal as parameters as well, and extending the diagnostics to those might be worth as well. (I fixed the parameters as well, but nothing prevents someone changing or introducing new places that violate this.)

I also did a bit of cleaning up in the source generator: there were two places where a local function parameter was "hiding" outer variable. That variable didn't need to exist and now there's two warnings less!

I think that's all?

AI disclosure time: There is no AI written code or message in this PR, however, since this issue touched a lot of places I did try out using an AI to:
* track down changes that happened between the original PR and now, for rebasing,
* validate I didn't miss anything anywhere,
* help me track down interactions where LSP doesn't help (like C#-C++ barriers),
* review my code,
* do more testing on the code. (There still isn't really much included tests to validate this part of the engine, so I thought it is better than nothing, but do keep in mind the tests were written and run by the AI (none of which is included in this PR) only on x86-64 (Fedora KDE) Linux, so please still give it thorough review.)
